migration.description: Persist short-lived Connector browser device authorizations and one-time exchange codes as hashes.
migration.release_unit_description: Phase-one Connector browser enrollment; a local callback proves the same Connector process that started the flow before a host credential is issued.

compatibility_assessment.reason: The migration adds device-enrollment endpoints and an additive short-lived table. Existing browser sessions, user credentials, host registrations and Connector gateway credentials remain readable; older candidates ignore the new table and endpoints.

durable_state.description: The table stores only hashes for the human verification code and one-time authorization code, the loopback redirect binding, browser state and expiry. Raw host credentials are never stored in this flow's database row.
durable_state.storage_implementation: PostgreSQL table managed by the embedded Goose application migration history; consumed rows remain as durable replay evidence and expire by query admission.

source_compatibility_range.to_program_version: Phase-one Connector browser-enrollment candidate containing migration 00017.
source_compatibility_range.compatibility_boundary: Earlier candidates continue to use existing host registration and credential rows and do not interpret connector_device_authorizations; the new candidate requires migration 00017 before enabling the device routes.

ordered_operations.description: Create connector_device_authorizations with one-way hashes, loopback redirect binding, browser authorization state and expiry.
Create the expiry index used to bound cleanup and admission scans.

rollout_signals: Goose records migration 00017 only after the additive table and expiry index commit.
Device start and authorization reject expired rows, and token exchange marks a code consumed while holding the row lock before issuing a host credential.

recovery.faulty_release_recovery: forward-repair-by-a-new-program-version; old host credentials remain usable and device enrollment can be disabled independently

validation: Focused in-process auth tests cover loopback redirect validation, state binding, one-time exchange and rejection of replayed authorization codes without a temporary database or external service.
SQL migration inspection confirms hashes, singleton-independent host enrollment references, expiry indexing and embedded Goose discovery.
Runtime acceptance must additionally prove a real database migration and browser OIDC flow before release promotion.
